Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $32 million class fund with automatic payments to all identifiable members. Brightline would separately pay up to $6 million in court-approved fees and expenses; any amount not awarded would go to the class. We are open to discussing the amounts, but automatic distribution is important given Brightline’s records.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that automatic payments are appropriate given Brightline’s records. We can offer a $30 million class fund plus up to $5 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with any unawarded fees going to the class. We would not agree to clear sailing.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your agreement on automatic payments and directing any unawarded fees to the class. We can narrow the remaining gap: a $31 million class fund and up to $5.5 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with no clear-sailing provision. All other terms would remain as discussed.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the movement and agree on automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and directing any unawarded fees to the class. To bridge the remaining gap, we propose a $30.5 million class fund and up to $5.25 million in court-approved fees and expenses.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $30.5 million class fund with automatic distribution, plus up to $5.25 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with no clear-sailing provision and any unawarded fees going to the class. We will work with you to prepare the settlement documents for court approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: The class has substantial potential recovery, but certification and trial remain uncertain. I will open with an automatic-distribution fund that delivers meaningful value to members. Fees should be separately stated, subject to court approval, with any reduction benefiting the class rather than reverting to Brightline.

The proposed $38 million total is within authorization and has court-friendly distribution and fee terms, but there is room to negotiate a lower total outlay. Offer $35 million while preserving automatic payments and unawarded fees for the class.

The defense offer provides substantial, automatically distributed class recovery and avoids fee-reversion concerns. With several rounds remaining, a modest counterproposal may improve the class recovery without jeopardizing a strong settlement.

The latest proposal is within authority and has court-approval-friendly distribution and fee terms, but there is room to narrow the remaining $1.5 million gap in round 2. Offer a midpoint while preserving those terms.

The $30.5 million automatic-distribution fund exceeds the $27.5 million trial-value estimate before accounting for certification risk, delay, and litigation costs. The separately paid $5.25 million fee is subject to court approval, and any reduction benefits the class. The terms avoid claims-made distribution, clear sailing, and fee reversion. Accepting is preferable to risking this favorable offer for a modest increment.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: I submit this declaration on behalf of Hargrove Lane LLP in support of preliminary approval. The parties reached the settlement through three rounds of arm’s-length negotiations after the case survived a motion to dismiss. Class relief and attorneys’ fees were discussed during the same negotiations; fees were not deferred until after class relief was agreed. The resulting settlement provides a $30,500,000 class fund, to be distributed automatically to identified class members without a claims process. Brightline will separately pay up to $5,250,000 in fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request, and any amount the court does not award will go to the class, not Brightline. The fund represents approximately 47.7% of the $64 million in disputed renewal charges. In my judgment, the guaranteed, automatic recovery is fair to the class in light of the risks of class certification and trial, the possibility of no recovery, and the delay of continued litigation. I request preliminary approval, subject to the Court’s independent review and consideration of class members’ responses.
